title: "If the other person won’t look": look at what?
highlight: If the other person won’t look
question: Two readers found that "It is its own reward" is a cliché and that "If the other person won’t look, you can’t make it mutual" doesn’t follow from the Bee story before it; a third read also found "It also became more permanent" reads as if the separation, not honesty, is the subject. My fix (it spelled out that any of those outcomes takes both people, and that the other person has to look at the truth with you) read AI by itself (https://www.pangram.com/history/2267fb23-7b39-47a6-9295-77ca69fefb79), so I’m trying again. If you’d like to say in a line what "won’t look" means here, or rewrite it, I’ll take it from there.
why: A passage that doesn’t follow, whose clear version reads AI so far (gate E291: the clear version stays the goal).
advice_note: I keep trying next turn either way.
block: Many people ask this question of honesty, but it’s unfair. Honesty doesn’t produce a certain outcome. It is its own reward. It might repair the relationship, open it, turn the romance into friendship, preserve the family through separation, or show you that ending it is better. Temporary separation helped Bee and I. It also became more permanent, although I’ve always thought maybe we would get back together in a few decades. If the other person won’t look, you can’t make it mutual. Then you have to decide what you can live with.

title: "The myths ... become real because we co-create them"
highlight: become real because we co-create them
question: Two readers found "The myths around romantic love become real because we co-create them" opaque. My fix ("We’re the ones who make the myths around romantic love real, by living as if they were true", with the four myths rebuilt) read AI by itself (https://www.pangram.com/history/9ad8bbbb-f6aa-4716-9179-ddd3d7ff5127); next I try changing only that first sentence and keeping the rest as the post has it. If you mean something more by "co-create", say so in a line.
why: A sentence that doesn’t say what it means, whose clear version reads AI so far.
advice_note: I keep trying next turn either way.
block: The myths around romantic love become real because we co-create them. We act as though jealousy proves love, permanent feelings can be promised, conflict should stay hidden, and the relationship failed if it ended. Then we suffer inside ideas that were never natural laws, and we walk blindly into our first, second, third, fourth, and fifth marriages!

title: "Asking the question out loud": which question?
question: Two readers found "Asking the question out loud is usually where it starts" names no question. My fixes named it (whether the romance needs less intensity, should become a friendship, or should end): the first read Human with a Low window (https://www.pangram.com/history/d05b3f9e-b70a-4eeb-8519-84aa6300e405), the next AI (https://www.pangram.com/history/049a89d6-54c5-40e3-a273-5e1ce4bb45f8). I’m trying again; if you’d word the question differently, say how.
why: A sentence that doesn’t say what it means, whose clear version doesn’t read Human High yet.
advice_note: I keep trying next turn either way.
block: It’s time to bring in other support once a partner has become the default caregiver and that’s taken for granted, or the romance could collapse under the burden. Maybe the romance actually does need less intensity, maybe it becomes friendship, or maybe it ends. Asking the question out loud is usually where it starts, though I can’t answer it for others (and couldn’t always answer it for myself).
